outputs.explanation: Panel A is a schematic diagram of breast anatomy plus a classification table, not a quantitative plot.
Panel B is a conceptual/schematic diagram outlining the study aim, not a data plot.
Panel C is a schematic illustration of the experimental setup (icons/cartoon), not a quantitative plot of data.
Panel D shows representative line traces of circadian signals over time; line plots are exempt from requiring overlaid individual data points.
Panel E is a correlation heatmap; heatmaps are exempt from the individual-data-points requirement.
Panel F shows growth curves (line plot of cell number vs. days) for representative models; line plots are exempt from requiring overlaid individual points.
Panel G shows dose-response line plots (growth inhibition vs. dose); line plots are exempt from requiring overlaid individual points.
Panel H shows gene expression and mutation heatmaps; heatmaps are exempt from the individual-data-points requirement.
Panel I shows PCA and parameter scatter plots where each dot already represents an individual data point/sample, satisfying the requirement.
